title: Console analytics ingest translation service (SDK/CLI -> canonical telemetry)
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: Console backend receives telemetry from multiple clients (JS SDK, Python SDK, CLI) with slightly different payload shapes and version headers. Current ingestion pipeline expects a canonical analytics contract; we rely on brittle upstream client upgrades and ad-hoc gateway fixes. This ticket scopes a new ingest translation service that performs runtime payload normalization, version negotiation, and lossless-to-lossy downgrades where acceptable so we can: 1) decouple client upgrade velocity from pipeline schema rollouts, 2) provide structured fallback behavior for older clients, and 3) centralize per-tenant transformation rules for privacy/compliance.
scope: Implement a small, horizontally scalable translation service sitting between the edge gateway and the analytics pipeline. Responsibilities: - Parse incoming telemetry envelope and client schema version header. - Validate payload against best-effort client-side schema. - Apply translation rules: field renames, flattening nested protobuf structures to canonical JSON, and KV-cache-safe prefix trimming. - Emit standard "canonical_v2" envelope downstream, attaching provenance metadata (original_version, applied_ruleset_id). - Support a configuration store to enable per-tenant lossy downgrades and sampling policies. - Provide metrics (translation latency, failure rate, rule matches) and tracing hooks for end-to-end debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Translation service deployed behind existing ingress with a feature flag.
>=95% of historical telemetry shapes are correctly mapped to canonical_v2 in staging (validated by golden set).
No more than 5% p99 latency increase to pipeline (measured on synthetic traffic).
Per-tenant rule toggles via console and a small config API are functional.
End-to-end tracing links from SDK event -> translated envelope -> storage exist in the console.
notes: Decision: prefer server-side deterministic translations over client shims to avoid repeated SDK releases for small contract diffs.
Trade-off: introducing translation adds a transformation hop; mitigated by batching and fast-path passthrough for already-canonical payloads.
Privacy: provenance metadata must avoid including PII; config store will allow redaction rules per-tenant.
Implementation options considered: lightweight Go service with protobuf descriptors vs. a Wasm-based transform runner; we chose Go for faster iteration and existing tracing infra.
